newsitem.title: UK: GEC gains after finance director quits.
newsitem.headline: GEC gains after finance director quits.

text.p: Shares in General Electric Co Plc rose in early trade on Thursday, against the weaker tone of the market overall, on news that its finance director David Newlands was to leave the industrial group, dealers said.
The stock was up 12p at 372 by 0754 GMT in active trade of just over two million shares.
Activity in the stock was frenetic enough to prompt a short periof of "backwardation" when the bid price displayed on the London Stock Exchange Seaq trading screen was above the "offer" price.
Analysts said Newlands' departure, announced late on Wednesday, had focused attention on next week's GEC results and an expected statement on strategic restructuring within the group.
"It has just focused minds on the restructuring next week and the result of the strategic review," said analyst Tressan MacCarthy at Panmure Gordon. "Maybe GEC is going to be more dynamic in future".

GEC said Newlands would leave the company on July 7 after assisting in the smooth handover of responsibility from long-serving chief executive Lord Weinstock to George Simpson, who joined from Lucas last year.

In a statement, GEC said Simpson "paid tribute to David Newlands' personal and professional qualities and his contribution to the company over the last eight years and wished him every success for the future".
However it gave no reason for the departure. A successor will be named in due course, GEC said.
